title: Airchecks, balance and song pluggers
summary: Thomas introduced airchecks to Cab, learned microphone balance from them, and remembers pluggers such as Bubbles Durgham.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: I taught them something else, too. We used to get airchecks. And I got the airchecks... That's how I learned a lot about recording. I found out where the mikes would sit, and we'd get the airchecks, and that way I found out

how the balance was. And I made the guys go out to the mike and play their solos, then come back and sit down. And that way we... I understand they took a lot of these airchecks and made records out of them.
Sure. I've got a lot of them here. I've got so many airchecks, old airchecks right off of acetates. I got some from (?).
And I'm the one that started it, because I knew the concern that did the airchecks, and I told Cab -- and it didn't cost but about ten dollars a night.
Yeah, fifteen dollars. But the one thing that I enjoyed about the band when we....
When Bubbles Durgham, which turned out to be Jackie Gleason's manager, a little short guy...
He was one of them guys I used to see come up there and talk to you. He was a song plugger. He used to (?) all the big movie stars.
And another guy that was the top man for Perry Como was a song plugger. I got to know him later. I had a way of knowing people that meant something. I don't know why. It's just a habit of mine.
